To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression and localizations of SSTRs were different in hormone-refractable prostate cancer (HRPC) compared with hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.
the expression of five SSTR subtypes in hormone-sensitive and HR PCa was evaluated immunohistochemical in 20 RPS with GS 3+3, 20 RPs 4+4 and 4+4+4, and 20 TURP specimens with HR PCA.
the expression of five SSTR subtypes was decreased in HR PCa, and this was especially evident in the glandular cytoplasm and nuclei, and also in smooth muscle and endothelia.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the expression of five somatostatin receptor (SSTR) subtypes in hormone refractory (castration resistant) prostatic carcinoma (HR PCa) and the localisation of the SSTRs in different tissue components in HR PCa.
the expression and localisations of the five SSTR subtypes in the various tissue compartments in the HR PCas compared with the hormone-sensitive PCas.
the role of SSTRs in PCa and the possibility of using them in the diagnosis and treatment of this disease.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of all five SSTRs was lower in the glands, smooth muscle and endothelium of HR PCa compared to GS 3+3 and 4+4 PCa.
the expression of all five SSTRs is decreased in the glands of HR PCa and increased in its smooth muscle and endothelia.
the expression and localisations of the five SSTRs are altered in HR PCa compared to hormone-sensitive PCa, which may have important clinical implications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in HR PCa, SSTRs are expressed at lower levels, and the expression of SSTR4 is the most prominent.

the SSTR expression and localisation in the glands of the HR PCa is lower than in hormone-sensitive PCa, and the expression and localisations of the SSTRs in smooth muscle and endothelium are similar to those in hormone-sensitive PCas.
the somatostain receptors are present in the prostate cancer tissue, but in a lesser extent than in hormone-sensitive prostate cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
SSTRs are expressed in the various tissue compartments of the HR PCa and may represent a target for the treatment of HR PCa with SSTR-targeting agents.
SSTRs are still expressed, albeit at lower levels, in HR PCa and thus may still be considered as targets for therapy.
the SSTRs are expressed in all the tissue components of HR PCa but at lower levels compared with hormone-sensitive disease.
